solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cross-channel boat, transport reversed into by judge

indicators.note: something reversed is turned round to run the other way, so these letters are read backwards
going into something means entering it, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: to carry goods is to transport them
a referee is the judge of a match, shortened to ref

explanation.surface: A ferry crossing the Channel, with some vehicle backed into it by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like a noun for a vehicle, but it is the verb: to carry. A ref is a referee, the judge of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A car ferry is a vessel that carries vehicles across water, such as the English Channel between Britain and France.

clue.text: Blooming cluster — Tom, his wife and kittens?

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
a man's wife and children are his family, his kin

explanation.surface: Tom the cat with his wife and kittens, a whole blooming cluster of a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' reads as a man's name, but it is a male cat; his household of wife and kittens is simply his family.
explanation.definitionFit: A catkin is a dangling spike of tiny flowers on trees like willow or hazel, a cluster in bloom.

clue.text: Fruit farmin’

blocks.note: first meaning: a dried grape
second meaning: a dropped-g form of rearing livestock or crops, written with an apostrophe

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the second word shows a dropped final g, and the clue wants the same dropped-g spelling of a synonym: raising crops is farming them.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a fruit; raisin' is a casual spoken form of raising, as in rearing animals or crops.

clue.text: Finally, people stop supporting comfortable living arrangement

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept
in a down entry, what supports something sits underneath it, so this piece is placed lower

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
cosy means snug and comfortable
to stem a flow is to stop it

explanation.surface: People finally stop paying for a comfortable home life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' reads as paying for someone, but in a down clue it puts the stop word beneath the comfortable word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecosystem is a community of organisms interacting with their environment, so it is a living arrangement in a biological sense.

clue.text: A New Year sober, I suspect? Look surprised!

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not to be trusted, so these letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sober on New Year? I find that suspicious, and you should look surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' seems to be the speaker doubting the sobriety, but it signals that the first five words, all fourteen letters, are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an eyebrow is the idiom for showing mild surprise or disapproval, a facial expression of disbelief.

clue.text: Grant set off in front

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A man named Grant set off ahead of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a person's name setting off in front, but it is the verb meaning to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to confer or give formally, which is what granting a favour or honour means.

clue.text: Heron nesting, in the end, in different tree

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept
being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter goes within the other piece
different means changed from how it was, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heron has ended up nesting in a different tree from usual.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree's letters are rearranged and the last letter of the nesting word drops into them after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a kind of white heron, a long-legged wading bird of the same family.

clue.text: In direct conflict, as one progresses along line of piggies?

definitions.text: as one progresses along line of piggies

blocks.note: first meaning: face to face in a confrontation

blocks.clueFragment: as one progresses along line of piggies
blocks.note: second meaning: moving one digit at a time along the foot

explanation.surface: Two rivals face off, while someone works down a row of little pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piggies' are toes, from the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market' counted on a child's toes; moving along them goes from one to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing toe-to-toe is an idiom for confronting someone directly at close quarters, as boxers do.

clue.text: Rover I’m not sure will go twice after stick

blocks.note: a wand is a thin stick
er is the sound of hesitation
the hesitation repeated a second time

explanation.surface: A dog called Rover dithers about going after a thrown stick twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' sounds like a dog's name fetching sticks, but it is the definition: someone who roams. 'After' places the doubled hesitation behind the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is someone who travels about without a fixed home, the same as a wanderer.

clue.text: Will you excuse me, huh?

blocks.note: first meaning: a polite apology
second meaning: a request to repeat something not heard

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase has two uses: apologising for a lapse, and asking someone to say again what was missed.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite formula serves both as an apology and as a request for repetition when puzzled.

clue.text: Capital of Lesotho is initially seen on holiday

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: a trip is a short holiday
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday visits Maseru, the capital of Lesotho.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for Lesotho's capital, but 'Capital' alone is the definition and 'of' is one of the three words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Pub drink, did you say? Jump the queue!

indicators.note: asking what was said points to the sound of the words rather than their spelling

blocks.note: a gin served at the bar of a pub

explanation.surface: Someone at a pub orders a drink, then pushes to the front of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin ordered at the bar, said out loud, sounds like the phrase for pushing in.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in is to push rudely ahead or interrupt, which is what someone jumping the queue does.

clue.text: Leader eliminated on Mediterranean island in aloof manner

indicators.note: the leader is the first in line, and eliminating it removes the opening letter

blocks.note: Sicily is the large island off the toe of Italy

explanation.surface: A political leader is ousted on a Mediterranean island, treated coolly by the voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a politician, but it is the first letter of the island's name, which is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting icily means behaving in a cold, unfriendly and distant way, just as aloofness suggests.

clue.text: Numbered group goes with them, I gathered

indicators.note: things gathered are collected up and bunched together anyhow, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A numbered group of people goes along with them, or so I gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' reads as 'I understood', but 'I' belongs to the letters and 'gathered' signals that they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome is a group of eight, best known from the eightsome reel, a Scottish country dance for eight people.

clue.text: Coronation artefact, rock cake?

blocks.note: first meaning: the block used when British monarchs are crowned
second meaning, whimsical: a rock made of a small baked teatime cake

explanation.surface: A rock cake, the crumbly British bun, is passed off as a relic from a coronation.
explanation.walkthrough: A rock cake is a real British bun, but here it is read as a rock of cake: a stone of a scone, a scone being a small plain cake. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone of Scone is the ancient Scottish coronation stone, placed under the throne when British monarchs are crowned.

clue.text: Cary Grant movie that’s funny is on, American film screened

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters come out in a strange order
something screened is hidden behind a cover, so these pieces are tucked inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
US is the abbreviation for American
pic is short for a picture, a film

explanation.surface: A funny Cary Grant movie is on, an American film showing on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screened' sounds like a film being shown, but it means hidden: the American film goes inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a 1941 Alfred Hitchcock thriller starring Cary Grant and Joan Fontaine, so it is one of his movies.

clue.text: Fish after fish served up — be a kipper elsewhere?

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means brought upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
coming after something means following it, so the first-named piece is sent second

blocks.note: eels are fish
the pout is a small sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: One fish served after another, a smoked herring dished up somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' suggests the smoked fish, in keeping with the fishy surface, but here it means someone having a kip, a sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep out is to spend the night away from home; a kipper here is one who kips, British slang for sleeping.

clue.text: Fuss over moot point, choice of candidate

indicators.note: moot means open to debate and unsettled, so these letters are not fixed in place
in a down entry, what is over something sits above it, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fuss about a debatable point in the selection of a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moot point' looks like a set phrase, but 'moot' is the signal to rearrange the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: When a party adopts a candidate it formally selects them to stand, so adoption is the choosing of one.

clue.text: Honorary title easy, as my lord is decorated

indicators.note: decorating something changes how it looks, so these letters are dressed in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An honorary title comes easily, since his lordship is a decorated man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorated' reads as a peer given honours, but it signals that the twelve letters before it are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Mayoress is the ceremonial title given to a mayor's wife or consort in British towns, an honorary rather than elected post.

clue.text: Requirement for mash taster after mashing!

indicators.note: mashing crushes things into a pulp, so these letters are broken up and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook's taster checks the mash once it has been mashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashing' fits the kitchen scene, but here it is the signal to scramble the letters of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taters is informal British slang for potatoes, the vegetable you need to make mashed potato.

clue.text: Marker and name on flag

blocks.note: a marker is a felt-tip pen
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone writes a name on a flag with a marker pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like it places the name on the flag, but it is taken as written and joins the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow triangular flag, traditionally carried on a knight's lance.

clue.text: Bud’s opening in high plant

indicators.note: an opening is the very start of something, so only the first letter is taken
being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter goes within the other piece

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a high is a state of euphoria

explanation.surface: A bud opens on a tall plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like an adjective for a tall plant, but it is the noun: a high is an elated feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is a large genus of plants, the spurges, including the poinsettia, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Weight and number for gas

blocks.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a weight
one is a number

explanation.surface: A chemist records a weight and a number for a gas sample.
explanation.walkthrough: OZ is the standard abbreviation for an ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a pale blue gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Portrait that is on the outside of publication

indicators.note: being on the outside of something means wrapping round it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is', from Latin id est
a mag is a magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A portrait is printed on the outside of a magazine, as a cover picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for 'that is' splits to wrap round the short word for a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a picture or likeness of a person, and an image is a likeness or representation.

clue.text: River in South America, alternatively in old Congo, drained

indicators.note: something drained has had its contents emptied out, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: or introduces an alternative
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A South American river, or alternatively one in the old Congo that has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: The Congo is a great river too, which tempts a solver to treat it as the answer's partner; here it only gives its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is one of the longest rivers of South America, flowing through Venezuela to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Cinema travelled to, start eating, rustling initially muffled

indicators.note: initially means in the first place, so a word gives up only its opening letter
something muffled is wrapped up to dampen it, so this piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: dive in is an informal call to begin a meal
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: At the cinema, people start eating and the rustling of sweet wrappers has to be muffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The rustle of wrappers fits the cinema, but its first letter is simply wrapped inside the phrase for tucking into food.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in is an open-air cinema where people watch from their cars, so it is literally driven to.

clue.text: Figure with sore back, painful to touch

indicators.note: going back means returning the way you came, so these letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: ten is a figure, a number
sore skin is red and inflamed

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore back finds it painful to the touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sore back' reads as an aching back, but 'back' signals that the word for sore is written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender describes flesh that hurts when pressed, the usual word for an area painful when touched.

clue.text: At once sister is working after beginning on itinerary

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a nun is a religious sister
taken as written
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A sister gets to work immediately once her travel itinerary begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At once' looks like 'immediately', but it means simultaneously, all together. A sister is a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in unison means doing them simultaneously, together at the same moment, which is the other sense of at once.
